content.title: Butler III Undergoes Successful Surgery
content.text: The Warriors concluded their 2025-26 season by splitting their two Play-In Tournament games and falling just short of a spot in the 2026 NBA playoffs. The Dubs turn their attention to an eventful offseason, where Head Coach Steve Kerr’s contract has expired, several players, including De’Anthony Melton, Al Horford and Kristaps Porzingis, are impending free agents and the team will have a lottery pick with the 11th-best odds at the first overall selection in the 2026 NBA Draft. During their exit interviews, players spoke about how much Kerr’s leadership has impacted the locker room and gave insight into their mindset ahead of contract negotiations. PLAYERS SHOW SUPPORT FOR KERR AS CONTRACT SITUATION LOOMSSteve Kerr just wrapped up his 12th season as the Warriors’ head coach and he has a decorated resume with the franchise, headlined by four championships, 604 career wins and 10 winning seasons. This season was a unique coaching challenge for Kerr, as he’s dealt with significant injuries to star players and did his best to maximize the potential of his younger, less experienced pieces. Gui Santos praised Kerr for the impact he has had on his career year, giving him the opportunity to prove himself and more responsibilities as the season went on. “Steve is a special guy for me,” Santos said. “He was the coach who gave me my first opportunity to play in the NBA. He's a guy who realized the dream for me — he was a big part of it. The way that he coaches, he understands the players very well, having played before.”“We were in Phoenix and Steve drew up a play for me for the first time,” Santos recalled. “I'm like, oh, that's different now. I'm not just being a guy that's crashing, an energy guy. He said, ‘throw him the ball. Gui, you're playing the pick-and-roll.’ That was my favorite moment when I realized how much my role had changed on the team.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 12:53Remaining Time 12:53Warriors Talk: Gui Santos 2025-26 Season Exit Interview – 4/20/26Brandin Podziemski expressed gratitude to Kerr for giving him a significant role from Day 1, an opportunity he admitted most young guys in the league don’t necessarily receive. “Definitely full of gratitude,” Podziemski said of his appreciation for Kerr. “He gave me a big opportunity that most young guys don't get, so definitely thankful on that end. Obviously, we would love to have him back.” Quinten Post referred to Kerr as a “legend” and a “brilliant basketball mind." “Steve is an absolute legend, of course and I've learned so much from him the last two years,” Post said. “Seeing how his mind works, seeing how he approaches the game. He loves this organization. He loves this team and he's absolutely brilliant. Everybody hopes that he's back. Also, he's been in this league for so long, he's had so much success — he needs to make his own decision and do what makes him happy.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 5:33Remaining Time 5:33Warriors Talk: Quinten Post 2025-26 Season Exit Interview – 4/20/26PLAYERS WITH DECISIONS TO MAKEThe Warriors have 11 2026 free agents and seven of them conducted exit interviews on Monday. All seven — Al Horford, De’Anthony Melton, Quinten Post, Pat Spencer, Charles Bassey, Nate Williams and Malevy Leons — expressed an affinity for the organization and were very much open to being back with the Warriors next season. Horford is confident that he can still play and contribute at a high level, but is currently weighing all of his options, including retirement. “I’ll take time to step back and have a clear picture, look at the outlook of the team, look at the future of the team and also see where I'm at and how I'm feeling,” Horford said of his outlook on free agency. “Fortunately for me, I'm healthy. I feel good. I still feel like I can contribute and play at a very high level. Now that everything kind of gets quiet, you know, it's something that I'll reflect on all that.”Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 13:07Remaining Time 13:07Warriors Talk: Al Horford 2025-26 Season Exit Interview – 4/20/26Horford has a player option, so the choice will be completely in his hands. Melton also has a player option and is taking a similar approach to his decision, but in the ideal world, he shared that he would “love to come back.”“I would love to come back,” Melton said. ‘I leave that type of stuff up to my agent and upstairs, but I would love to. You've got to give yourself time to decompress and see everything that's going on, let the dust settle.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 7:22Remaining Time 7:22Warriors Talk: De'Anthony Melton 2025-26 Season Exit Interview – 4/20/26Bassey is an unrestricted free agent who made a great first impression on the Warriors, working his way up from the G-League affiliate in Santa Cruz. Bassey believes he’s proven himself to be an NBA player, instantly clicking with Stephen Curry offensively and learning from Al Horford defensively. “Showcased that I'm an NBA player for sure,” Bassey said. “It's been tough this year going to different teams, but seeing how different players approach the game has been great. I've picked a lot of brains. I’ve shown that I can play — I belong in this league. Steph told me that we play like we've been playing for years. I talk to Al about what he brings defensively. These guys have rings. It's just been great playing with them, picking their brains and getting better.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 6:28Remaining Time 6:28Warriors Talk: Charles Bassey 2025-26 Season Exit Interview – 4/20/26The Warriors have contract options on Post, Spencer and Williams. They are also eligible to negotiate a rookie extension with guard Brandin Podziemski, who expressed a desire to remain with the Warriors long-term. “I want to be here for the long-term,” Podziemski said. “It's always special having the team that drafted you, so hopefully we can get something done.”Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 10:34Remaining Time 10:34Warriors Talk: Brandin Podziemski 2025-26 Season Exit Interview – 4/20/26Podziemski believes seeing how his teammates’ rookie extension negotiations played out was a valuable foresight for his situation. “Seeing Jonathan [Kuminga] and Moses [Moody] do two different things for me helped, just seeing the pros and cons to both sides,” Podziemski said. “I don't think one is better than the other, but seeing that as a teammate and seeing how they handled both situations, I think it's going to help me.”
